title: Why sourcing and picking edges vanish for investors and winning allocations is what matters
summary: Ryan Hoover argues that the traditional VC edges of sourcing and picking startups are eroding because public signaling, discovery tools and AI make every deal visible and evaluable by everyone. What remains is winning the allocation, which depends on helping founders and earning access.

principles.text: Sourcing and picking edges are eroding; winning the allocation is what matters most.
principles.quote: In other words, there’s no edge in sourcing and picking in the near future. All that matters is winning.

principles.text: Everyone will see every deal as founders signal publicly and tools surface them.
principles.quote: It’s obvious when a founder is preparing to raise. They launch on Product Hunt. They get loud on X

principles.text: AI will evaluate deals and founders more thoroughly than humans can.
principles.quote: It will comb through data rooms more thoroughly than any human could, instantly evaluating comps, the market, and the team’s background.

principles.text: Spend less time hunting and analyzing, more time helping founders; that is the input to winning the next deal.
principles.quote: They can spend more time helping founders\[1\], the core input into their ability to win the next deal.

principles.text: Proprietary, non-public data is the exception where sourcing and picking can still produce alpha.
principles.quote: Investors that have truly proprietary, non-public data may still have alpha in sourcing and picking.

principles.text: Reputation is earned by helping founders; brand is shaped by perception.
principles.quote: Reputation is what you earn by helping founders, but brand is informed by perception, for better or worse.
